text.en: Two batsmen both average 50 runs, but one scores steadily while the other swings between 0 and 100. The mean alone cannot tell them apart - we need a measure of spread.

Range = largest value - smallest value. It is quick but depends only on two numbers.
Variance measures how far values are on average from the mean: variance = sum of (x - mean) squared / n.
Standard deviation is the square root of the variance, written sigma. It has the same unit as the data.
Shortcut: variance = (sum of x squared)/n - (mean) squared.
A small standard deviation means the data are close to the mean; a large one means they are spread out.
If every value is increased by the same number, the standard deviation does not change; if every value is multiplied by k, it is multiplied by k.
Coefficient of variation = (sigma / mean) x 100 percent, used to compare the consistency of two data sets.

why.en: Take the square root of the variance.

prompt.en: Why do we need the standard deviation as well as the mean?

requiredIdeas.en: Mean shows the centre not the spread
SD measures spread around the mean

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking a larger mean means larger spread

points.en: Variance = average squared deviation; SD = its square root.
Adding a constant leaves SD unchanged.
Lower coefficient of variation = more consistent.
